Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation reduced depression scores more than placebo at 38-40 weeks of gestation.
Sentence: "While, the vitamin D group had greater reduction in depression scores than the control group at 38-40 weeks of gestation (p = 0.01) also, at 4 and 8 weeks after birth (p < 0.001)."
Measured as: depression score (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression scale) at 38-40 weeks of gestation
Population: Pregnant women in Shiraz, Iran, 18 or older, gestational age 26-28 weeks, baseline depression score 0-13, no history of mental illness
Intervention: Vitamin D3 2000 IU daily from 26-28 weeks of gestation until childbirth
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 169
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is an uncontrolled single-arm case series in Parkinson's patients with a multi-vitamin product, while Study B is a placebo-controlled RCT of vitamin D3 alone in pregnant women; the results differ mainly by design and comparator.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","comparator"],"detail":"design: case series, single-arm, no control vs randomized placebo-controlled trial; comparator: none vs placebo"}
